title: Hostless NCCL pipelining and staged KV-prefetch scheduler for tensor-parallel runtime
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: TP jobs at 4+ GPUs frequently hit comm/compute synchronization stalls when host-side coordination is used to serialize NCCL phases and to trigger KV-cache prefetches. These stalls manifest as repeated micro-idles in the p99 tail for short sequences and during dynamic batch spikes. This PR introduces a "hostless" NCCL pipelining path and a staged KV-prefetch scheduler that work together to overlap collectives with compute while bounding extra memory and avoiding premature prefetches.

Summary of changes: Adds a new comm path that moves NCCL collective kick-offs to per-GPU worker threads and relies on CUDA events and intra-node progress to avoid round-trip host barriers; implements a staged KV-prefetch pipeline that prefetches KV slabs at two levels (speculative window + confirm window) driven by the continuous-batching controller; introduces a small kernel reordering heuristic that opportunistically advances short reduction kernels ahead of long compute kernels when their dependency DAG allows it; exposes three runtime knobs (tp.hostless_enable, tp.prefetch_window, tp.kv_slab_max_inflight) and safe fallbacks to existing behavior.

Implementation notes: The new hostless path is implemented in src/runtime/comm/hostless_nccl.cpp and wired from the TP scheduler in src/runtime/tp/pipeline_scheduler.cpp. Per-GPU worker pools are sized by default to (num_gpus * 2) but tunable via runtime config. KV prefetch is implemented in src/runtime/kv/prefetch_coordinator.cpp with a two-stage state machine: SPECULATE -> CONFIRM -> COMMIT. The continuous-batching controller in src/runtime/batching/continuous_controller.cpp now tracks a short-term batch-size histogram to decide prefetch aggressiveness; this avoids overfetch during heady request bursts.

Compatibility & safety: The hostless path is behind the flag tp.hostless_enable=false by default. When enabled the scheduler performs liveness checks and will automatically revert to host-mediated orchestration if CUDA event progress stalls are detected for 100ms. The staged prefetch caps memory via tp.kv_slab_max_inflight and will never exceed slab cap; if prefetch fails, the system falls back to synchronous fetch with instrumentation.

Performance: On internal TPU-like clusters (8xA100 equivalence) we see: median throughput +6-12% for short sequence chat workloads (seq_len<=128), p99 latency reduced by 22% for small microbatches, and sustained throughput improvement of ~9% under mixed seq workloads. Memory overhead measured at steady-state is +3-7% depending on prefetch window. Benchmarks are in perf/bench-tp-hostless/benchmark-2024-11-30.log (summary in perf_benchmarks).

Rollout plan: Feature rollout attenuated: enable on canaries (owners: infra/perf team) with tp.hostless_enable=false for 48h, traffic-gradient to 10% then 30%. Telemetry added to telemetry/tp_hostless_metrics.{promql,json} to track evictions, fallback events, and prefetch-inflight counts. Quick rollback via feature flag.

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for state transitions in prefetch_coordinator and for fallback behavior under simulated progress stalls. Integration tests in e2e/tp/validate_prefetch.yaml simulate dynamic batching and assert no deadlocks. A new flaky test marker was added for nccl-progress-related tests to reduce noise.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached (docs/design/tp-hostless-prefetch.md) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Perf benchmarks - [x] Telemetry dashboards - [x] Rollout plan

Related: Linear items ENG-4210, ENG-4278. See also RFC: rfc/tp-comm-prefetch.md.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the initial heuristic conservative: it prefers reduced risktaking and clearly signals fallback events in telemetry. Future work planned: hostless cross-node progress (wire up NCCL P2P progress heuristics), automatic prefetch tuning by workload fingerprinting, and kernel co-scheduling with weight-aware priority queues.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Nice isolation of the worker pool. Two comments: (1) prefer a bounded task queue to avoid unbounded memory spikes when request rate jumps, (2) can we add a debug-only tracepoint when fallback triggers?
Aisha Patel: Added bounded queue with high-water backpressure and a debug tracepoint event (telemetry/tracepoints.md). PTAL.

Linus Berg: Observed a small hang on our internal CI when forcing simulated CUDA stall; seems related to the event wait timeout. Suggest increasing the watchdog to 150ms in the test harness and asserting fallback path triggers within 200ms.
Aisha Patel: Adjusted test harness timeouts and added an explicit test for fallback event emission.
Sofia Cheng: Approve after CI rerun. Verified perf numbers on canary run; prefetch_inflight metric useful.
ci_status: pass (one flaky nccl progress test retried)
release_notes: Introduce experimental hostless NCCL pipelining and staged KV-prefetch scheduler behind feature flags. Improves p99 and throughput for short-sequence TP workloads. Defaults off; enable via tp.hostless_enable.
testing_instructions: 1) Boot canary with tp.hostless_enable=true on a 4+ GPU node group. 2) Monitor telemetry: prefetch_inflight, hostless_fallback_count, tp_kernel_reorder_hits. 3) Run e2e/tp/validate_prefetch.yaml. 4) If fallback_count > 0 for >5% requests in 10min, disable the flag and open ENG ticket.
perf_benchmarks: memory overhead - steady +3-7% depending on prefetch_window
notes: Conservative initial rollout; operator-visible metrics added. The hostless path reduces host wakeups by coalescing NCCL kick-offs and leveraging GPU-driven progress on supported drivers. Cross-node hostless progress is deliberately excluded from this change to reduce blast radius.
